## README.md

[![CI](https://github.com/mithudso/stickysites/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mithudso/stickysites/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

## docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

StickySites is a Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) that injects a floating note workspace into every web page. Notes live in `chrome.storage.local` with optional AES-256-GCM encryption. There is no hosted StickySites service or telemetry. Optional native messaging mirrors to-dos into `TODO.md`. An optional loopback daemon relays snapshots to paired LAN computers or to a shared/cloud folder selected by the user.

## docs/COMPONENTS.md

"Namespace" = the `window.StickySites.*` object a classic content script attaches; "Exports" = ES module exports.

## docs/DEVELOPMENT.md

Runbook with verification steps: `runbooks/load-and-reload-extension.md`.

## docs/INSTALLATION.md

The global to-do list can mirror into a Markdown file through a native-messaging host that lives outside this repo (`~/.claude/skills/todo/`). Install it for every browser profile:

## docs/MCP.md

StickySites ships no Model Context Protocol server or MCP operation registry. Its runtime is an extension plus an optional Python peer daemon/CLI. The optional native host is installed outside this repository. Native, loopback, paired LAN, and shared-folder boundaries are inventoried in [external-calls.md](external-calls.md).

## docs/SECURITY.md

StickySites runs as a Chrome Extension on every web page. It injects DOM into untrusted host pages, stores user notes locally with optional encryption, and (optionally) exchanges the to-do list with a local native-messaging host. An optional daemon exposes loopback HTTP and authenticated LAN HTTPS/UDP discovery, and can use a shared/cloud folder.

## docs/TESTING.md

Use the Node version in `.nvmrc` that satisfies `package.json` engines, then `npm ci`.

## docs/caching-and-optimization.md

The extension has no CDN or hosted database. It stores data in `chrome.storage.local`; the optional daemon also stores a local snapshot and uses peer HTTP ETags/folder caches.

## docs/external-calls.md

StickySites operates no hosted service or telemetry. Optional native and loopback calls leave the browser. The peer daemon can then use a paired LAN or a user-selected shared/cloud folder; a cloud provider may transfer files outside the LAN. Browser APIs such as storage, tabs, windows, alarms, and context menus are inventoried in `integrations-and-assumptions.md`.

## docs/integrations-and-assumptions.md

StickySites has no hosted telemetry. Its optional boundaries are a local native host, loopback daemon, paired LAN peers, and a shared/cloud folder selected by the user.

## docs/known-issues.md

Format: symptom → cause → workaround → files.

## docs/logging.md

The extension uses browser consoles rather than a logging framework or hosted telemetry. The optional Python daemon separately appends to `~/.stickysites/peer.log` (or `STICKYSITES_HOME/peer.log`). The external native host owns its own diagnostics.

## docs/onboarding.md

A path from checkout through a verified change.

**Runtime**: none.

## docs/runbooks/encryption-lock-and-recovery.md

Vault design: `docs/SECURITY.md`. Code: `src/content/crypto-content.js`, `src/shared/note-writer.js`, popup Settings.

## docs/runbooks/load-and-reload-extension.md

**Precondition**: an explicitly requested live browser check, a checked-out repo, and passing automated checks. This runbook is not a requirement to activate an extension during automated maintenance; use an isolated test profile and preserve active user sessions.

## docs/runbooks/peer-sync.md

Two or more machines on the same LAN keep their StickySites notes converged through the peer helper (`peer/stickysites-peer.py`). Design and security model: `peer/README.md`.

## docs/runbooks/release-packaging.md

**Precondition**: `main` green in CI; `manifest.json` and `package.json` carry the same new version (`npm run lint` enforces this); `memory.md` / `prompts.md` updated.

## docs/runbooks/todo-sync-troubleshooting.md

The global to-do list optionally syncs with a local `TODO.md` through the native-messaging host `com.mitch.todo_bridge` (`src/shared/todo-bridge.js`, driven by `src/background/service-worker.js`). Without the host the extension works normally and the list stays local.

## docs/wiki/index.md

StickySites is a browser extension with optional local native messaging and a Python peer helper. There is no hosted application server or shipped MCP server.

## peer/README.md

Keeps two or more laptops' StickySites notes converged over a paired LAN or a shared/cloud folder you select, without a hosted StickySites service. A tiny Python daemon (stdlib only, Python 3.9+) runs on each machine; the extension talks to it on loopback, the daemons talk to each other on the LAN.

## store/README.md

Submission assets and instructions for publishing StickySites on the Chrome Web Store. The account owner completes the publishing steps. The package version comes from `manifest.json`; rebuild and verify the kit for each release.

## store/listing.md

Paste-ready text for every field in the Developer Dashboard. Character limits are the store's; counts are given where they matter.

## store/permissions-justifications.md

One text box per permission in the Developer Dashboard. Each entry below is written to be pasted verbatim. Keep them factual — reviewers compare against the code.
